feature: Trim, as a tool in the ordinary window
summary: The last open question in the video design is answered: a recording no longer gets its own little window, and trimming becomes a tool you pick in Crop's slot, with its handles on the clip and its Cancel and Trim on the same glass capsule a crop ends on. Trim-and-send stays exactly as many moves as it is today.
setup: Nothing to install. Three things to read and one page to walk: docs/design/video-surface.md §10, http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#video-shell block 05, and UX-PATTERNS D20. The primitive is comp-video §08.

try.do: Look at the trim bar that ships today: Reset, Cancel, Done, and two glyphs standing beside them.
Open video-shell block 05 and find the capsule over the canvas. It says In, Out, how much is kept, then Reset, then Cancel and Trim.
try.shotNote: This is the mock page in a browser, not the app. The surface is a design and nothing has built it yet; the first picture is a real window capture.

try.do: Look at the tool bar in the same picture: Trim is lit, in the slot Crop was in, and V would leave it.
Look at the clip in the timeline: both handles are up, and the frames outside the in and the out are drawn beside it with their durations.
Read the two cards under the window: what the recording window says today, and what the app already says when a mode ends.
Read §10.3 in docs/design/video-surface.md, the four-row table, and check that trim-and-send is the same number of moves as today.
Read §10.5, the awkward corners, and say whether any of the five answers would surprise you.

evaluate: Crop is C. Pressing C again now hands you Trim in a document with time. Is that a helpful pair, or would you rather press C and always get Crop?
The button says Trim rather than Done. Reading it cold, does it say what pressing it does?
A recording opens with Trim already in hand. Does that feel like the app knowing what you came for, or like being put in a mode you did not ask for?
The handles are on the clip's bar at the bottom, not on the picture. Is that where your hand goes to shorten a recording?
The frames you trimmed off stay drawn beside the clip. Is that reassuring, or is it clutter on a timeline you wanted clean?
rough: NOTHING IS BUILT. This is the design pass for the video work, so every picture but the first is a mock page in a browser. The build is a-document-can-have-time, which now carries two acceptance items for it.

The Trim tool's glyph is a small rounded rectangle and does not obviously say trim at a glance. The icon library has ic-trim and this design uses it rather than drawing a new one; whether it reads is worth a look on the real bar.

Crop and Trim sharing C is the marquee pair's mechanism, and a box and an ellipse are far more alike than a crop and a trim. The slot shows which one is in hand and the capsule names the mode, and that may not be enough. It is the first evaluate question for that reason.

The capsule floats over the canvas, and in a video window the transport is already a band under it. At a small window those two plus the tool bar are three stacked things; --mb-lift exists so the capsule clears the bar, but nobody has drawn the narrow case.
§10 settles what trim is and not what send is. What Export offers a recording is video-share and is still unwritten.
The panel is still 189 points over in a video document at the largest window. Unchanged by this pass and not video's to fix.
